question: Can many infinite percolation clusters coexist before one becomes unique?
idea: On the specified nonamenable quasi-transitive graphs, the manuscript claims the threshold for having infinite clusters is strictly below the threshold for having just one. That leaves a genuine interval of edge probabilities with infinitely many infinite clusters. The graph assumptions distinguish this from ordinary Euclidean-lattice behavior.
why: The study of randomness and large collections of interacting parts. It connects individual random events with collective patterns.

exactClaim: Proves $p_c\lt p_u$ for Bernoulli bond percolation on every infinite connected locally finite nonamenable quasi-transitive graph, resolving the Benjamini–Schramm nonuniqueness conjecture. Thus there is a nonempty range of probabilities with infinitely many infinite clusters. A stronger operator bound also establishes the critical triangle condition. )
